Thought: When active metals react with compounds containing active hydrogen, they typically displace the hydrogen atoms, releasing hydrogen gas. This is a common reaction in chemistry where metals react with acids or water to produce hydrogen gas. 

For example, when zinc (an active metal) reacts with hydrochloric acid (which contains active hydrogen), the reaction produces zinc chloride and hydrogen gas:

\[ \text{Zn} + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{ZnCl}_2 + \text{H}_2 \]

Thus, the gas that is formed is hydrogen.
